common--projects-title: A little of what I've done from childhood to today
main--bio-1: I'm a professional developer who also studied finance, economics, sales, marketing, business, investments and design, so I build technology that makes business sense.
main--bio-2: I started in tech at 10 and have lived from it since 16. Today I'm building two agencies under Gadmin: Gadmin Sell and Gadmin Conty.
main--presentation-title: Presentation: Who I am and What I do.
projects--gadmin-conty-content: Conty is an agency, not an app or a chatbot: your business data, turned into strategy. Businesses share their income, sales, expenses and restock costs, and we deliver detailed reports with strategic analysis (margins, peak hours, average ticket, offers that work) and a clear decision to take the same day. Hours saved, and a team they don't have to hire.
projects--gadmin-gvp-content: Gadmin GVP is the software I built in La Guaira while serving after the double earthquakes, for the whole GVP organization: medical consultations, morbidity records, statistical analysis of patients and donations, and inventory. The software is private, but I also built the organization's website (the link below). Made so the work on the ground wouldn't get lost in the chaos of each day.
projects--gadmin-sell-content: Gadmin Sell is a WhatsApp sales agency: commercial attention 24/7, without hiring. We don't just reply, we guide every conversation to the close, offer the upgrade, combo or add-on that raises the ticket, follow up with whoever didn't buy, and pass to a person only what needs one. Built for appointment, table and visit businesses, always in the client's voice and by their rules.
projects--sorteos-mdb-content-1: I created this Md'B Raffles website so my wife could run as many raffles as she wanted, and participants could register automatically and easily.
projects--sorteos-mdb-content-2: Additionally, a random roulette wheel was linked to select the winner by automatically taking the numbers of all participants.
projects--gadmin-legacy-content-2: Improved was renamed Gadmin. This was the software that saved entrepreneurs time in the complete management of their business, inventory, invoicing, etc. Several entrepreneurs used it and were happy with it, so we migrated to the new Gadmin, which still includes a large part of the functionalities of this software.
projects--file-content-1: I've built this JavaScript library that gets the extension and/or mimeType of a filename or path.
projects--file-content-2: Its purpose is to make the job of managing file extensions in the backend easier.
projects--adventjs-1: A repository where I shared the solution of the 24 challenges of AdventJS, an initiative by @midudev where a JavaScript challenge is published every day of December until the 24th of December.
projects--adventjs-2: As a competition lover, I had to do it. I took that year to enjoy it, and since then, I do it every year.
projects--improved-website-app-1: Thanks to the Bokados project, I was able to create a mobile app to make the management of local businesses, inventory, invoicing, etc. more efficient.
projects--improved-website-app-2: With this foundation, the 2023 version of Gadmin was born, where the tool was greatly improved. I was happy when we added ticket printing, barcode scanning... Little by little, I was understanding where I wanted to go with Gadmin.
projects--bokados-1: A bakery wanted to have a price menu updated in real time with the dollar exchange rate in Venezuela.
projects--bokados-2: This was the beginning of the Gadmin Startup, when I didn't even know yet that I wanted to make people's lives easier on such a scale.
projects--improved-website-1: A web design agency that makes websites for the world, my dream was always to create an editor so that people could create websites without needing to know how to program, but the agency was a good start.
projects--improved-website-2: This was the beginning of Gadmin, when I didn't even know yet that I wanted to make people's lives easier on such a scale, I just wanted to allow everyone to create websites.
projects--calculadora-1: I got tired of calculating PayPal commissions, so I built this calculator in less than 2 hours to calculate the commissions of my payments that I received and made.
projects--calculadora-2: I'm not a fan of PayPal commissions. Today I don't use it, if you can go away, do it.
projects--narubyond-1: As a child, I was excited to create video games. I learned by using an existing project and wrote about it while learning English by translating the entire game.
projects--narubyond-2: I remember spending days trying to understand what a piece of code did. It's fun to look back and think that today I've taught so many people to understand code like that.
projects--ngn-1: After my first project, I wanted to experiment with something more complex, it was quite fun and I learned a lot more about programming.
projects--ngn-2: 1 year later I left the project and dedicated myself to full stack web development, since it was something that I started to like even more.
projects--correfution-1: Corre Fution is a topdown game that is quite difficult to play that I made in a RandomJam#2 where we competed by creating a game in 24 hours.
projects--correfution-2: I was already professionally developing web applications, since I had been experimenting with JavaScript for 5 years, the previous projects were lost. (To programmers it usually happens that we lose an entire hard drive 😭)
business--kunzapp-content-1: A short but rich experience helping Kunzapp in its first steps launching their MVP and presenting at the Platanus Ventures Demo Day, where they raised USD $150,000 in capital.
business--kunzapp-content-2: Together with the team, I built the best tool to achieve savings, visibility, and control of all your organization's SaaS.
business--smartcompliance-content-1: A small team and I transformed a backend built on monolithic architecture into a microservices architecture using AWS Lambdas, increasing server performance, scalability, and efficiency, while reducing infrastructure costs by more than 60%.
business--smartcompliance-content-2: The best part was the team, people who enjoyed the day-to-day and with whom you could share very fluidly.
business--gadmin-content-1: I founded Gadmin to run the sales and finance side of small businesses and give their owners their time back. With Gadmin Sell we close sales on WhatsApp 24/7, and with Gadmin Conty we organize every income and expense so each decision has a number on it.
business--gadmin-content-2: I build the systems and AI automations behind both teams, so the business sells more, sees clearly where every cent goes, and grows without being glued to the chat. 😉
business--wekan-content-1: As part of WeKan's engineering teams, I modernize legacy infrastructure and systems in record time, powered by AI agents and proprietary modernization platforms, for companies in India and around the world.
business--wekan-content-2: I work remotely from Venezuela, blending startup agility with enterprise-grade engineering discipline: progressive architecture, cloud and infrastructure migrations without disrupting operations.
about--story-content-1: I wrote my first code at 10 years old. At 16 I decided to make a living from it, and I haven't stopped since. I started with no university, no resources and not even reliable internet, but I didn't want to stop.
about--story-content-2: Then I realised that great software alone doesn't grow a company. So I studied what companies really run on: finance, economics, sales, marketing, business, investments and design.
about--story-content-3: That mix is why I don't just write code. I understand the numbers, the customer and the market behind the product, and I use AI to build faster and more efficiently.
disciplines--title: What I studied and use every day
disciplines--dev-desc: Full-stack products, cloud and AI automation.
disciplines--finance-desc: Reading the numbers behind every decision.
disciplines--economics-desc: Pricing, incentives and how markets behave.
disciplines--marketing-desc: Positioning and content that reach the right people.
disciplines--investments-desc: Thinking in returns, risk and long-term value.
disciplines--design-desc: Products people understand and enjoy using.
services--intro: I don't sell hours of code. I work on what your business needs to grow, and I choose the technology that gets you there.
services--1-body: Internal tools, apps and automations that remove repetitive work and let your team focus on what matters.
services--2-body: Websites, funnels and tools that capture, follow up and close customers with less friction.
services--3-body: Systems for accounting, invoicing, inventory and reporting, so you always know where the business stands.
services--4-body: Help deciding what to build, in what order and for whom, before you spend money building it.
method--intro: Code is just the tool. This is the process I follow with every company and every product.
method--1-body: Your customers, your numbers and the real bottleneck, before any technical decision.
method--2-body: Build it, buy it or automate it with AI tools that already exist. Whatever is fastest and cheapest for the result.
method--3-body: Small, working releases you can use and judge, not months of silence.
method--4-body: We track what changed in your results and iterate until the numbers move.
ventures--parent: Both agencies are part of Gadmin, my company.
ventures--sell-body: An agency that helps businesses sell more with systems, automations and AI tools built around how they sell.
ventures--conty-body: An agency that brings order to the finances of small businesses with clear, automated accounting and reporting.
content--title: I create content about <hl>business</hl> and technology
content--body: How to make businesses and people grow faster and more efficiently with all the new AI technologies and tools that we can use, or build ourselves.
content--image-alt: Orlando recording content about business and technology
teaser-courses--body: One course to build products with AI and understand the engineering underneath. Four modules, the same class for every level.
teaser-impact--title: I use what I have to help <hl>people</hl>
teaser-impact--body: When earthquakes hit La Guaira, Venezuela, I moved there to help. Technology is only worth it if it serves people.
impact--meta-description: How Orlando Briceño uses his skills, time and resources to help people, from the La Guaira earthquakes to today.
impact--title: Technology is only worth it if it serves <hl>people</hl>
impact--lead: I care about people's wellbeing, and I use my time, skills and resources to bless them. This is what that looked like after the earthquakes in La Guaira.
impact--closing-title: The same mindset I bring to companies and students
impact--closing-body: Whether I'm building software for a company, teaching a class or helping in a crisis, the goal is the same: leave people better than I found them.
contact--content-1: Did you like something I'm building?
contact--content-2: If you want to be part of the Gadmin team or you like to talk about an idea or project, don't hesitate for a second to write me.
footer--title: A bit more about me to reward you for making it this far
footer--content-1: If I seem ambitious to you, you're not wrong. But even so, my family is above everything else. When I'm not trying to change half the world with Gadmin, I'm spending time with my wife.
footer--content-2: One thing you can be sure of: I will always be very honest, although sometimes you might not like it.
certification--practical-javascript-desc: A course that made me review daily practice and I learned some good practices.
certification--professional-javascript-d: I delved into advanced JavaScript, closures, hoisting, event loops, and more craziness with asynchrony.
certification--nodejs-desc: I reinforced some concepts while studying this course, they touched on how frameworks work that you use daily and don't understand their background.
certification--professional-git-desc: Here I really learned Git methodologies to streamline teamwork efficiently.
certification--html-css-desc: After 12 years using HTML and CSS, you still learn new things when you focus on learning.
certification--logical-thinking-desc: The important thing about this course was putting it into practice, problem solving is part of everyday life.
certification--time-management-desc: I learned techniques to manage time and improve productivity. I recommend reading the book Deep Work, by the way.
certification--emotional-intelligence-de: I learned about emotional intelligence, an important area of life and still very little mentioned.
stories--intro: When the earthquakes hit La Guaira, Venezuela, on June 24, 2026, I went to help. I arrived on June 28. This is the story.
stories--start-body: I started with no resources and no money. Only myself and a computer. My wife's support was vital: with her I grew in every part of life, into the person I am today.
stories--start-alt: A young Orlando Briceño working at a computer on the floor of his home
stories--start-two-alt: Orlando Briceño and his wife at a small desk with two computers in a modest room
about--carnet-alt: Orlando Briceño holding his ID card
stories--zone-body: This is what I found when I arrived. There were bodies in the rubble, and also teams and civilians working together to rescue people and bring some peace back to families, hoping to find someone still alive.
stories--zone-alt: Collapsed buildings in La Guaira, with rescue teams and civilians in the rubble
stories--kids-body: With my wife, in the free time we had left, we brought some joy to the children: singing lessons and small activities so that, even for a moment, they could laugh.
stories--kids-alt: Orlando Briceño holding a paper butterfly during a moment of play with children
stories--wck-title: Those who held the country up
stories--wck-body: Huge organizations helped the whole country, and GVP, the group I was part of. World Central Kitchen was one of them. Without that help, many days would not have been enough.
stories--wck-alt: Orlando Briceño beside a World Central Kitchen volunteer
stories--barber-body: Eating, getting a haircut, sleeping: for months I did all of it there. I moved completely so I could help as much as possible. I got sick several times from the polluted air. It was still worth every second. I cried with many people, and I also made others laugh in the middle of their grief.
stories--barber-alt: Orlando Briceño getting a haircut during the months he spent at the epicenter
stories--amda-alt: Orlando Briceño holding his AMDA interpretation certificate
stories--gvp-alt: Orlando Briceño holding his GVP certificate of recognition
stories--mcdonalds-alt: Orlando Briceño holding his McDonald's recognition
recognitions--intro: Recognitions I received from the organizations I worked alongside while helping people in La Guaira.
recognitions--amda-body: I communicated in English with Japanese members of AMDA, including its president, Dr. Takushi Sato. I helped them with their tasks and with support at the so-called McDonald's Hospital, run entirely by GVP.
recognitions--amda-certificate-alt: AMDA certificate of recognition presented to Orlando Briceño
recognitions--gvp-body: I built software for the whole organization: consultations, morbidity records, statistical analysis of patients and donations, and inventory. I wanted the work on the ground not to disappear into the chaos of each day.
recognitions--gvp-certificate-alt: GVP certificate of recognition presented to Orlando Briceño
recognitions--mcdonalds-body: McDonald's recognized the effort of everyone who collaborated with GVP. They wanted to give us something simple, and enormous: they called us heroes.
recognitions--mcdonalds-certificate-alt: McDonald's certificate calling Orlando Briceño a hero
courses--meta-title: AI Builder with an engineering base | Orlando Briceño
courses--meta-description: One live course to build products with AI and understand the engineering underneath: systems, the web, language models, and an MVP with payments and automations. Three support levels, the same class.
courses--subtitle: This is not a course to become a full-stack developer. It is for building products with AI and understanding the engineering that holds them up: systems, data, APIs, and deploy. Four modules, the same class for all three levels. Only the support changes.
courses--cta: Reserve your seat in the course
courses--outcomes-intro: You are not buying hours of class. You are buying a way of thinking, an AI workflow, and a product you can show, use, and charge for.
courses--outcome-1-short: You think in systems, not loose lines
courses--outcome-1-body: You stop writing loose code. You learn to think in systems, set up context, and direct tools like Cursor or Claude so they build exactly what you need.
courses--outcome-2-body: You connect language models, structure their replies, and tie your business logic to WhatsApp, payments, and databases using webhooks and tools like n8n.
courses--outcome-3-short: An MVP with payments and metrics
courses--outcome-3-body: You finish the course with a working product: interface, database, and an AI layer, published, with a payment gateway like Stripe and basic usage metrics.
courses--audience-yes-1: You are starting from zero and want a clear route instead of a pile of random tutorials.
courses--audience-yes-2: You want to build a real product with AI, like a light SaaS, a catalog, or an assistant, instead of stopping at syntax.
courses--audience-yes-3: You are a founder or freelancer who wants to automate orders, payments, or support, for example over WhatsApp.
courses--audience-yes-4: You want a mentor who understands both technology and business.
courses--audience-no-title: This is not for you if
courses--audience-no-1: You only want passive recorded videos with no one to ask.
courses--audience-no-2: You are looking for a shortcut with no practice.
courses--audience-no-3: You are not willing to ship something every week.
courses--live-intro: The class exists so you are not left alone with videos. I am in the session with you, and every week has something to finish.
courses--live-1-body: Each class runs 1.5 to 2 hours: the idea, then your questions, in the same session.
courses--live-2-body: Between classes you get a practical guide for the week. You practice and ship, instead of watching and forgetting.
courses--live-3-body: Every module ends with a result the next one uses: the map of the web, a deployed app, a connected automation, and, at the end, the MVP of your product.
courses--path-intro: The whole group sees all four modules, in the same class, at the same time. Each module ends with a result that feeds the final project.
courses--mod-mindset-focus: Think in systems instead of loose lines of code.
courses--mod-mindset-topics-1: The programmer's new role: from writing code to acting as architect and conductor.
courses--mod-mindset-topics-2: A modern AI workflow: how to use tools like Cursor or Claude, structuring prompts and context so they build exactly what you need.
courses--mod-mindset-topics-3: The mental map of the web: what the client is, what the server is, how data travels (HTTP, APIs, WebSockets), and where information lives.
courses--mod-mindset-goal: you direct AI as an architect and you can see how data travels across the web.
courses--mod-foundations-focus: Only what actually matters to understand a real project.
courses--mod-foundations-topics-1: Essential frontend: HTML as a data structure, modern CSS (Tailwind or base styles) for clean interfaces, and the visual logic the user handles.
courses--mod-foundations-topics-2: Backend and databases: what a relational database is (like SQLite or Turso), what an API is, and how the server processes information safely.
courses--mod-foundations-topics-3: Deploy and cloud: how to put an app on the internet in minutes with modern platforms (Cloudflare Pages, Workers) without fighting complex servers.
courses--mod-foundations-goal: you understand a real project end to end: interface, database, API, and deploy.
courses--mod-stack-focus: Tools that multiply how fast you can build.
courses--mod-stack-topics-1: Architectures built for speed: light databases, serverless environments, and offline-first patterns.
courses--mod-stack-topics-2: Language model integration: how to connect AI APIs, structure responses, handle context, and build simple conversational agents.
courses--mod-stack-topics-3: Automation and connectivity: tools like n8n or webhooks to connect business logic with WhatsApp, payment gateways, and databases.
courses--mod-stack-goal: you connect a language model and an automation to your product.
courses--mod-project-name: From idea to a real product
courses--mod-project-focus: A working product, start to finish, during the course.
courses--mod-project-topics-1: Product definition: how to shape an app that solves a real problem, like a light SaaS, a catalog with WhatsApp orders, or a sales-flow assistant.
courses--mod-project-topics-2: AI-guided development: build the frontend, connect the database, and add the AI layer with assistance, step by step.
courses--mod-project-topics-3: Launch and monetization: how to shape an MVP, connect a payment gateway like Stripe, and read basic usage metrics.
courses--mod-project-goal: a live MVP, with payments and metrics, built from start to finish.
courses--mentor-title: Real information from someone who builds with it
courses--mentor-body-1: I'm Orlando. I started in tech at 10, have lived from it since 16, and I studied finance, economics, sales, marketing, business, investments and design.
courses--mentor-body-2: I'm building two agencies, Gadmin Sell and Gadmin Conty, so what I teach is what I use with real clients. You get real mentoring, not theory.
courses--price-intro: Prices in USD. It is one course: all three levels sit in the same live classes and go through all four modules together. The level only changes how close the support is.
courses--tier-low-desc: Live group classes with me, once a week, plus that week's practice guide.
courses--tier-mid-desc: Everything in Essential, plus a private channel for support between classes.
courses--tier-vip-desc: Everything in Standard, plus one monthly 1:1 mentoring session.
courses--full-note: All four modules, from mindset to a live product. One payment up front. Every level sees the same class.
courses--week-1-body: Once a week, 1.5 to 2 hours. Theory and questions in the same room.
courses--week-2-body: A practical guide, sized so you can finish it without burning out.
courses--week-3-body: You pick a support level and pay for the whole course up front. You join the same classes as the rest of the group.
courses--faq-1-a: No. The course starts from zero and the whole group moves through all four modules together. The level does not change which class you see, only the support.
courses--faq-2-q: Do I leave with something I can show?
courses--faq-2-a: Yes. You finish with a real product online and the practice of having built it with AI. That is what you can show a client or in an interview. I can't promise a job, because that depends on your effort.
courses--faq-3-q: What if I miss a class?
courses--faq-3-a: You keep the practice guide for that week and can ask your questions in the next session or, on the Standard and VIP levels, in the private channel.
courses--faq-4-a: You pay for the whole course up front, at the level you choose: Essential, Standard, or VIP. We confirm everything by email.
courses--faq-5-q: Do I get support between classes?
courses--faq-5-a: Yes, on the Standard and VIP levels, through a private channel. VIP also includes one monthly 1:1 mentoring session.
courses--faq-6-q: What language are the classes in?
courses--faq-6-a: The classes can be taught in Spanish or English. Tell me which you prefer when you reserve your seat.
courses--faq-7-a: Small, because the class is live and I want to answer everyone's questions.
courses--final-title: Seats stay small because the class is live
courses--final-body: Tell me the level you want and I confirm your seat in the course by email.
courses--wa-full: Hi Orlando, I want to reserve my seat in the course AI Builder with an engineering base.
